title: Walt Disney World Opens in Florida
description: The Magic Kingdom and its Florida resort opened to the public near Orlando, realizing Walt Disney's vision for a second, larger theme park.
longFormSummary:
• Planning began quietly in 1959, with Walt Disney personally scouting the swampy Bay Lake site by plane in 1963 to secure enough land to control the area around the park, unlike at Disneyland.
  • Land was assembled secretly through proxy companies such as the "Reedy Creek Ranch Corporation" to avoid inflating prices.
  • The Magic Kingdom opened on a weekday with modest crowds of around 10,000, with two resort hotels and two golf courses also ready.
  • A three-day grand dedication followed later that month, on October 23-25, 1971.

dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "The Magic Kingdom, Polynesian Village Resort, and Contemporary Resort Hotel opened on October 1, 1971."

title: TAKRAF Commissions the First F60 Overburden Conveyor Bridge at Welzow
description: VEB TAKRAF completed the first F60 lignite overburden conveyor bridge at the Welzow open-pit mine, creating what is still recognized as the largest mobile land machine ever built.
longFormSummary:
• The F60 is 502 meters long, up to 80 meters high and 240 meters wide, weighing around 13,600 tons in operating condition.
  • It strips overburden from lignite seams so open-cast coal mining and the power plants that depend on it can continue.
  • Four F60 units still work today at Jänschwalde and Welzow-Süd in Brandenburg and at Nochten and Reichwalde in Saxony.
  • A fifth, retired F60 near Lichterfeld-Schacksdorf is now open to visitors as the Bergbau-Erlebnispark F60.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia's Overburden Conveyor Bridge F60 article dates the first unit's construction to 1969-1972 and entry into service at the Welzow open-pit mine to 1972, without a specific day.

title: Magnavox Releases the Odyssey, the First Home Video Game Console
description: Magnavox released the Odyssey in the United States in 1972, the first commercial home video game console, designed by Ralph Baer’s team at Sanders Associates. The Age of Mass Production cites it as the start of mass-produced video game hardware.
longFormSummary:
• Ralph Baer's engineering team at defense contractor Sanders Associates designed the hardware, which Magnavox then completed and brought to market.
  • Magnavox released the Odyssey in the United States in 1972, unlocking different games via swappable circuit cards rather than true cartridges.
  • It is recognized as the first commercial home video game console, predating Atari's arcade hit Pong, which used a near-identical tennis-style game later that year.
  • The Odyssey sold around 350,000 units before being discontinued in 1975, kick-starting mass consumer demand for home video game hardware.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Sources disagree on the exact month of release in 1972 (Wikipedia gives September, other historical accounts give August), so only the year is treated as confirmed.

  • Draws from Talbingo Dam and discharges to Jounama Pondage, near Talbingo, New South Wales.

title: Sydney Opera House Officially Opens
description: Queen Elizabeth II officially opened the Sydney Opera House, capping fourteen years of construction that ran a decade late and far over its original budget.
longFormSummary:
• Danish architect Jørn Utzon won an international design competition in 1957 with sketches for the building, beating 232 other entries from 32 countries.
  • Construction started in 1959 before the roof design was finalised, so the first support columns had to be torn out and replaced once engineers worked out how the iconic shells would actually be built.
  • The sail-like roof shells were eventually resolved as sections of a single sphere, one of the first times a building project leaned on computers to run structural analysis.
  • The finished building arrived roughly a decade behind schedule and about fourteen times over its original AUD $7 million budget, at a final cost of AUD $102 million.
address: Sydney Opera House, Bennelong Point, Sydney NSW, Australia
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "the Sydney Opera House was officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II."

title: NIED's Large-Scale Rainfall Simulator Opens in Tsukuba
description: Japan's National Research Institute for Earth Science and Disaster Resilience completed its hangar-sized Large-Scale Rainfall Simulator in Tsukuba, letting scientists recreate extreme storms on demand to study landslides and flooding.
longFormSummary:
• Built at NIED's Tsukuba headquarters following a string of destructive typhoons, the facility uses over 2,000 nozzles suspended 16 metres up to generate rain closely matching real storm droplet sizes and speeds.
  • Inside the roughly 75m by 15m hangar, researchers build full-scale soil slopes and test flood-resistant housing designs under controlled, repeatable rainfall.
  • The simulator is mounted on rails so it can move between test zones, letting the same rig study slope failure, flooding and building resilience without being rebuilt each time.
  • Decades on, its data still feeds early-warning sensor design for landslide-prone areas across Japan.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "The facility was established in 1974, following a series of destructive typhoons."

title: First Prefab Panel Goes Up at Berlin-Marzahn, Founding Europe's Largest Housing Estate
description: A VEB Wohnungsbaukombinat Berlin construction brigade set the first concrete panel of a WBS 70 apartment block at Marchwitzastraße on 8 July 1977, starting what became Europe's largest prefabricated housing estate with 103,000 flats built in 15 years.
longFormSummary:
• The Peter Zeises construction brigade of VEB Wohnungsbaukombinat Berlin set the first WBS 70 concrete panel at Marchwitzastraße 35-45 on 8 July 1977.
  • The building topped out just two months later, on 2 September 1977, and its first tenants moved in on 18 December 1977.
  • Over the following 13 years the GDR built roughly 103,000 apartments across Marzahn using the WBS 70 prefabricated panel system, making it the largest such estate in Europe.
  • Chief architect Roland Korn led the design team chosen through a 1973 competition.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Berlin newspaper reporting on Marzahn's 40th anniversary states the construction brigade Peter Zeises of VEB Wohnungsbaukombinat Berlin set the first panel of a QP 71/WBS 70 building at Marchwitzastraße on 8 July 1977.

title: Citicorp Center's Secret Structural Fix Wraps Up
description: Engineers quietly finished weeks of overnight welding that fixed a hidden wind-bracing flaw in Manhattan's Citicorp Center, averting a possible collapse.
longFormSummary:
• A 1978 re-analysis uncovered a flaw in the wind-bracing system of the newly built tower that could have caused it to topple in a strong storm.
  • Structural engineer William LeMessurier disclosed the defect to Citicorp and city officials, triggering a covert nightly welding campaign to reinforce roughly 200 bolted joints.
  • Crews worked after office hours from August into October 1978, while Hurricane Ella's approach in early September briefly threatened to cut the repair short.
  • The building, now known as Citigroup Center at 601 Lexington Avenue, remains a landmark case study in engineering ethics and disclosure.
address: 601 Lexington Avenue, Manhattan, New York, NY
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Repairs were completed in October 1978."

title: Volvo Assembles Its First F7 Truck at New River Valley
description: In September 1982, Volvo Trucks built the first Volvo-branded truck ever assembled in North America, a Volvo F7, at its newly acquired New River Valley plant in Dublin, Virginia. The factory has produced every Volvo truck sold in North America ever since.

title: Scheuerle Debuts the Self-Propelled Modular Transporter
description: German heavy-vehicle maker Scheuerle Fahrzeugfabrik developed and launched the Self-Propelled Modular Transporter (SPMT), the modular, multi-axle hauler that became the industry standard for moving exceptionally heavy loads. Its name is now used generically across the heavy-transport industry.
longFormSummary:
• Scheuerle Fahrzeugfabrik (now TII Scheuerle), based in Pfedelbach, Germany, developed and launched the SPMT in 1983.

  • SPMTs can move loads sideways and diagonally as well as forward and backward, using Powered Hydrostatic Driven Tractor Modules.
  • The SPMT name, originally Scheuerle’s, is now used industry-wide for this class of heavy transporter.

title: Five Pacific islands lost to rising seas as climate change hits
description: Using time series aerial and satellite imagery from 1947 to 2014 of 33 islands, along with historical insight from local knowledge, we have identified five vegetated reef islands that have vanished over this time period and a further six islands experiencing severe shoreline recession.
longFormSummary:
• A 2016 study published in Environmental Research Letters examined how sea-level rise and wave exposure interact to erode low-lying reef islands in the Solomon Islands, a region with some of the highest rates of sea-level rise in the world.
  • Researchers analyzed aerial photographs from 1947-1962 and satellite imagery from 2002-2014 across 33 islands, combined with wave-energy hindcast data and radiocarbon dating of trees.
  • Five vegetated reef islands vanished entirely and six more lost over 20% of their area during the study period.
  • Erosion accelerated sharply on the more wave-exposed Isabel islands, where shoreline recession rates rose from about 0.1% annually (1947-1962) to 1.9% annually (2002-2014), compared with minimal change in the more sheltered Roviana region, where wave energy was twenty times lower.
  • At two Isabel sites, erosion destroyed villages that had existed since at least 1935, forcing community relocations.
  • The study concludes that sea-level rise and high wave exposure interact synergistically, meaning local wave conditions can dramatically amplify a coastline's vulnerability to climate-driven erosion.

title: California Law Now Requires All Smartphones to Have Built-In Kill Switches By July 2015
description: A California bill requiring all smartphones sold in the state to have antitheft technology installed was today signed into law by California governor...
longFormSummary:
• California's SB-962 "kill switch" bill, signed into law by Governor Jerry Brown on August 25, 2014, requires all smartphones sold in the state to include built-in antitheft technology, effective July 2015.
  • The technology must be able to render a lost or stolen phone inoperable to unauthorized users, survive a hard reset or OS downgrade, and prevent a stolen phone from being reactivated on a wireless network without the original owner's authorization, while remaining reversible for the legitimate owner and enabled during initial device setup.
  • Apple's iPhones already satisfy the requirement through Activation Lock, tied to iCloud accounts, while other manufacturers like Samsung and Microsoft would need to build comparable features.
  • The law sits in a broader context of anti-theft efforts aimed at reducing smartphone theft in major cities: Minnesota had passed a similar law, several manufacturers had voluntarily committed to kill-switch features by July 2015, and a federal Smartphone Theft Prevention Act was under consideration that could extend the requirement nationwide.

title: Fifty-six percent of California voters approved Proposition 64 Legalizing Marijuana
description: Proposition 64, The Adult Use Marijuana Act, permits adults over 21 years of age who are not participating in the state’s medical cannabis program to legally grow (up to six plants, including all of the harvest from those plants) and to possess personal use quantities of cannabis (up to one ounce of flower and/or up to eight grams of concentrates) while also licensing commercial cannabis production and retail sales
longFormSummary:
• Proposition 64, California's Adult Use Marijuana Act, took effect November 9, 2016 and legalized cannabis for adults 21 and older.
  • Adults may possess up to one ounce of flower and/or eight grams of concentrate, cultivate up to six plants at home (keeping the full harvest from those plants), and gift up to one ounce to another adult without payment.
  • Violations outside those limits carry penalties: possessing more than 28.5 grams of flower or 8 grams of concentrate, growing more than six plants, or selling/delivering cannabis without a license are each misdemeanors carrying up to six months in jail and a $500 fine, while illegally manufacturing concentrates using volatile chemicals is a felony punishable by three to seven years in prison and up to a $50,000 fine.
  • For minors under 18, most possession and distribution violations are treated as infractions requiring drug counseling and/or community service rather than jail time, though violations on school grounds carry enhanced penalties.
  • The law also created a path for people to petition to have past marijuana convictions expunged, and left California's existing medical marijuana program in place alongside the new adult-use rules.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild lands top spot on IGN's 10 Best Legend of Zelda Games of All Time
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild reinvented a 30-year-old series in a way we rarely see. After Skyward Sword offered a slightly more linear, story-driven campaign than most fans were used to, Breath of the Wild readjusted dramatically in the opposite direction. Suddenly you could go anywhere and climb anything in any order you wanted, and goodness gracious was there a whole lot to choose from.

There are plenty of fair criticisms to throw at Breath of the Wild, with common ones being its lack of traditional Zelda dungeons and items. But what’s truly impressive is how much it maintained the heart of a Zelda game even as it altered nearly every system around it. To a certain extent, Zelda has always been about exploration and choice, and Breath of the Wild simply leaned into and enabled those aspects of itself above all else, now making the world a place that would react to those choices as well. There’s just so much to see, so many people to meet and secrets to find hidden throughout this long-since devastated version of Hyrule.

title: Intel patches nine-year-old enterprise CPU vulnerability
description: Intel has just patched a vulnerability which has been open and exploitable in all its enterprise targeted Core processors - for the last nine years. Since 2008 Intel's business-focussed PC processors have shipped with Active Management Technology (AMT), Intel Standard Manageability (ISM) and Small Business Technology (SBT) features - all useful features for remote management.
longFormSummary:
• Intel released a firmware patch on May 2, 2017 fixing a critical vulnerability that had existed since 2008 in the manageability features of its enterprise-targeted Core processors — Active Management Technology (AMT), Intel Standard Manageability (ISM), and Small Business Technology (SBT), spanning firmware versions 6.x through 11.6.
  • The flaw let an unprivileged attacker seize control of these remote-management features, exploitable by anyone with Metasploit on the same local network, or remotely if port 16992 was reachable.
  • Security researcher outlet SemiAccurate had warned about risks in Intel's vPro technology as early as 2012 and reportedly flagged the issue to Intel executives repeatedly over five years without resolution, drawing criticism for the company's slow response, especially since exploitation was suspected to already be occurring in the wild.
  • Because the fix must be distributed by individual motherboard vendors rather than applying universally, many older systems whose vendors no longer support them may never receive it; Intel published a mitigation guide for those left unpatched.
  • Ordinary consumer PCs were not affected, as the vulnerable features are specific to business-oriented hardware.

title: A New Doubly Charmed Particle Has Just Been Discovered in CERN
description: For many years, physicists have been aware of the existence of this doubly charmed particle because of current physical theories. However, nobody has been successful in observing the particle and it is only now that the baryon with two heavy quarks has been distinctively detected. longFormSummary:
• On July 7, 2017, the LHCb (Large Hadron Collider beauty) collaboration at CERN announced the discovery of a new particle designated Xi_cc++ (Ξcc++), made up of two charm quarks and one up quark.
  • It is the first confirmed observation of a baryon containing two heavy quarks — all previously known baryons contained at most one — and at roughly 3,621 MeV it is nearly four times heavier than a proton.
  • Physicists had theoretically predicted such doubly-charmed particles for years based on the Standard Model but had never directly observed one until this measurement.
  • LHCb physicist Giovanni Passaleva said the particle "will provide a unique tool to further probe quantum chromodynamics," the theory of the strong nuclear force that binds quarks together, and researchers expect it to help refine predictions of how quarks interact.
  • The team anticipates finding related particles in the same family, including baryons containing two beauty quarks or combinations of beauty and charm quarks, and plans to continue searching for them.

title: Horizon Forbidden West Review  - IGN

The result is a fantastic open-world action-adventure that, despite falling into a couple of its old habits, emphatically delivers on the promises made five years ago.

title: New Ceramic Coating Could Make Hypersonic Air Travel a Reality
description: The new coating is 12 times more effective than current ceramics. Dennis Muilenburg, CEO of Boeing has said that hypersonic passenger jets could be in the air within the next ten years. These aircraft would cut travel times by up to 700 percent. This would mean a flight from Shanghai to New York would be reduced from 15 hours to just two.
longFormSummary:
• A team of Chinese and British scientists -- from the University of Manchester, the Royce Institute, and China's Central South University -- developed a new carbide-based ceramic coating using a manufacturing process called reactive melt infiltration, reinforcing zirconium carbide with a carbon-carbon composite.
  • The resulting coating is about 12 times more resistant to oxidation and degradation than current ceramics, which matters because aircraft flying at Mach 5 generate surface temperatures between roughly 3,600 and 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.
  • The article ties the research to industry momentum around hypersonic passenger travel: then-Boeing CEO Dennis Muilenburg predicted such jets could become reality within the next decade or two and cut travel times by up to 700 percent, turning a 15-hour Shanghai-to-New York flight into roughly two hours, while Boom Supersonic's CEO Blake Scholl noted five airlines had placed orders following the Paris Airshow.
  • Lockheed Martin and DARPA are also mentioned as pursuing hypersonic vehicle development.
  • The article is careful to note that commercial viability remains uncertain given the very high operating costs involved, and that the coating's more immediate applications are for spacecraft re-entry as well as potential future civilian hypersonic aircraft.

title: Elden Ring Review  - IGN
description: In the 87 hours that it took me to beat Elden Ring, I was put through an absolute wringer of emotion: Anger as I was beaten down by its toughest challenges, exhilaration when I finally overcame them, and a fair amount of sorrow for the mountains of exp I lost along the way to some of the toughest boss encounters FromSoftware has ever conceived. But more than anything else I was in near-constant awe – from the many absolutely jaw-dropping vistas, the sheer scope of an absolutely enormous world, the frequently harrowing enemies, and the way in which Elden Ring nearly always rewarded my curiosity with either an interesting encounter, a valuable reward, or something even greater. FromSoftware takes the ball that The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild got rolling and runs with it, creating a fascinating and dense open world about freedom and exploration above all else, while also somehow managing to seamlessly weave a full-on Dark Souls game into the middle of it. It shouldn’t be a surprise to anyone that Elden Ring ended up as one of the most unforgettable gaming experiences I’ve ever had.

title: Gran Turismo 7 Review - IGN

title: Kirby and the Forgotten Land Review - IGN

His ability to transform himself into all sorts of shapes and sizes aside, the games he’s in often experiment with new settings and gimmicks as well – whether it’s rolling a limbless Kirby with the DS stylus in Canvas Curse, piloting mechs in Planet Robobot, or fundamentally changing how he transforms in Epic Yarn. title: The Quarry Review - IGN
description:
Like many of developer Supermassive’s previous games, The Quarry is clearly made both by and for people who love horror movies. From the start, it slowly builds tension and atmosphere, getting you invested by constantly asking you to make small decisions that will guide its teenage cast of potential murder victims. By the time the blood started flying, every choice felt like one more step in a rolling disaster, and that made it nearly impossible to put down. When I went back to replay it again, however, it was impossible to ignore just how non-interactive much of The Quarry actually is. As a spiritual sequel to Until Dawn, it's a better movie, but a worse game.

You follow the story of nine camp counselors who get stuck in the woods for one more night at the end of the summer, with nothing to do but throw one last party before they go back to their lives. There's something stalking them from the treeline (because of course there is) and your choices determine which, if any, of the counselors will be able to survive the night. This setup layers three fairly textbook horror plots on top of each other as you progress, but you can tell that Supermassive Games had a lot of fun figuring out how to connect them together. When you play, you may think you're in one type of horror movie, but you're often in another.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge Review - IGN
description:
Growing up as a child of the 90s, whenever I stepped into an arcade, I’d always do a walk around to see what they had before putting my quarters into any machines. This usually didn’t last very long because as soon as I saw a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles cabinet, I’d shout to my friends “They got Turtles!” and we’d rush on over.

It’s abundantly clear that the developers at Tribute Games share a similar love for the 90s TMNT beat-em-ups. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder’s Revenge is nothing but unwaveringly reverent to the classic 1989 Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Arcade game, and more prominently, 1991’s Turtles in Time. Best of all, it transforms the arcadey quarter-munching design of combat into something much more skill forward while still maintaining the same button mashy appeal. Put simply, Shredder’s Revenge is a prime example of how to breathe new life into a classic arcade beat-em-up.

title: As Dusk Falls Review - IGN
description: At first glance, Two Rock, Arizona is merely a backwater town occupied by little more than tumbleweed and a few rows of houses. But very little is as it first appears, and all it takes to reveal As Dusk Falls’ many layers of storytelling depth is one small, decades-spanning tragedy. And it’s all about the story, since this is a choose-your-own-adventure-style graphic novel that cleverly pulls ideas from games like Telltale’s The Walking Dead series and 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim. Each member of this voice-acting cast of unique and interesting characters has their own, often conflicting emotional stakes that accelerate the story in seemingly hundreds of logical and intelligently connected directions. Through the powerful and often far-reaching consequences of your own actions, this small town is gradually unveiled as a powder keg full of secrets, vices, and familial bonds that run far deeper than any outsider is initially led to expect.

title: Stray Review - IGN
description:
A delightful cat-based platforming adventure in a cyberpunk world worth exploring.

Silent protagonists are nothing new in video games, but Stray certainly pushes that concept to an interesting place. Part platformer, part traditional adventure game, this cyberpunk world full of neon-soaked robots transforms into a giant jungle gym from your perspective, which is just one foot off the ground. The concept of putting you in the paws of an average cat may be a silly one on the surface, but Stray uses that furry vehicle to tell a genuinely compelling story with some entertaining action along the way. Not all of its ideas land on their feet, but it was impossible to shake the fuzzy feeling it gave me right from the adorable opening minutes.

title: China rolls out a further 1 trillion yuan in economic stimulus ($146 billion dollars)
description:
Among the allowances, state policy banks were given an additional 300 billion yuan ($44 billion) focused mainly on financing infrastructure projects. Tight rules were announced alongside the measures that require the projects to be profit-making and targeted.

Local governments were given the green light to use more than 500 billion yuan ($73 billion) of existing special bond quotas and were promised reduced financing costs through interest-rate changes.

Amid an energy crisis sparked by severe droughts and heat waves, the cabinet said central-government-run electricity firms will be allowed to sell 200 billion yuan ($29 billion) in special debt to ensure adequate energy supply.

title: Splatoon 3 Review: Single-Player  - IGN
description: Historically, Splatoon’s single-player campaigns have focused on acclimating you to the waters of its much more frantic and churning multiplayer battle modes. Splatoon 3’s campaign — dubbed The Return of the Mammalians — starts in territory so familiar that I was initially worried I was about to spend the next several hours slogging through tutorials on fundamentals I’d learned two games ago. Thankfully, the rug was quickly pulled out from under me, leading to a brand-new take on the series’ hub world design mixed with some of the best ideas of Splatoon 2’s Octo Expansion. Splatoon 3 boldly let me decide on whether or not to blaze my own path toward any of its 70 bite-sized, inventive missions, and choose where to go next when exploring its fuzzy ooze-filled world. A lot of the enemies I found there were unchanged from previous Splatoons, but I had a great time navigating the large variety of objectives all the way to the campaign’s explosively satisfying finale.

description: Poland opened the Vistula Spit Canal, a new $450M channel letting ships reach the port of Elbląg without passing through Russian-controlled waters near Kaliningrad.

  • The canal officially opened on September 17, 2022, deliberately timed to the 83rd anniversary of the Soviet invasion of Poland.

title: Gatwick Completes Main Runway Resurfacing
description: Gatwick Airport finished an overnight resurfacing of its main runway's busiest sections in September 2022, using a leaner method that cut the job to half the usual time and material.
longFormSummary:
• Gatwick's main runway hadn't been resurfaced since 2012, but a full traditional repaving was judged wasteful since much of it still had years of life left.
  • Crews instead resurfaced only the most heavily trafficked touchdown and taxi-off sections, working in narrow overnight windows between flights.
  • The approach used about 40,000 tonnes of asphalt versus the roughly 140,000 tonnes a full repave would need, cutting cost and carbon significantly.
  • The project wrapped up in September 2022, in around six months versus the year a conventional resurfacing would typically take.

title: A Plague Tale: Requiem Review - IGN

You liked massive swarms of rats? Well, how about we increase the number of them by a degree of 1,000! You enjoyed a gruesome and harrowing journey that tested the limits of your emotional resilience? Great, let’s increase your personal suffering by 200%! This follow-up to one of my favorite action-adventure games of the previous console generation turns the dials up to 11 in practically every way, and overwhelmingly benefits from those escalations despite sometimes being a bit heavy on the nihilism. With improved stealth action mechanics, a fantastic (and deeply depressing) story, and graphics that had me gawking, A Plague Tale: Requiem is an impressive glow up that’s easily worth the immense horrors it subjected me to.

title: Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope Review - IGN
description:
When a game hits on a good idea, some developers are content to play it safe for the sequel, making a few refinements but largely stick to what worked the first time. That totally makes sense. But Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope is not that kind of sequel; even though Mario + Rabbids: Kingdom Battle surprised us all with its smart XCOM-style tactics in Nintendo clothing, this followup maintains its best ideas but reinvents itself to the point where it immediately feels very different. It’s bigger and better in nearly every way, with a more freeform and customizable take on combat and an almost completely rethought overworld that’s much less linear and absolutely packed with puzzles. The story’s all over the place and the Switch can’t always handle everything smoothly, but it’s a fantastic game that can be played as either an enjoyable cakewalk or a deep, demanding tactical challenge, all while maintaining its zany sense of humor.

Picking back up in the post-Rabbid invasion Mushroom Kingdom, things immediately get even weirder when a giant manta ray from space arrives to cause trouble. The story is actually one of Sparks of Hope’s few missteps: the original’s trans-dimensional blending of Mario characters and goofball Rabbids is completely absurd, but it kind of makes sense in its own way. This time, though, the completely unrelated enemy spreads what’s effectively Ganon’s corrupt ooze with eyeballs from Breath of the Wild everywhere, and most but not all of her minions are also Rabbids for some reason? Also we have a spaceship for traveling between literal worlds? It makes Kingdom Battle look grounded in reality by comparison, which is something I never thought I’d say about that game. I wasn’t expecting deep lore or anything, but it’s kind of a mess. It does consistently have some pretty good jokes, though, so at least I was chuckling as I was scratching my head.

title: Bond Street's Elizabeth Line Station Finally Opens
description: London's Bond Street station opened to Elizabeth Line services, closing out the last and most delayed piece of the Crossrail project.
longFormSummary:
• Bond Street was the one station left unfinished when the rest of the Elizabeth Line opened in 2022, because it doubled as the recovery point for the tunnel boring machines used across the project.
  • Cramped access in Mayfair meant heavy machinery had to move in and out through undersized shafts, slowing work considerably.
  • Post-Grenfell fire safety rules forced already-installed cladding to be ripped out and redone partway through construction.
  • Crossrail eventually took delivery of the station in-house from its contractor after Covid-19 made the dense underground site impossible to safely re-mobilise on the original schedule.
address: Bond Street Station, Mayfair, City of Westminster, London, UK
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "the first Elizabeth line services arrived at the station at 05.47" on Monday, 24th October.

title: Bayonetta 3 Review - IGN
description: I hold the Bayonetta series’ combat in such high esteem that I’d consider it in the top five or so combat systems of all time, right next to the Devil May Cry, God of War, Ninja Gaiden, and Batman Arkham games. It’s just incredible to look at, feels equally amazing to play, and is jam packed with opportunities for style and creativity thanks to the wide assortment of wild weapons at your disposal. Bayonetta 3 just further cements its legacy, strutting out with a surprising sequel in that it actually takes a lot of risks with changing up its established formula in an effort to revitalize a combat system that only slightly evolved between the first two games. Fortunately those risks pay off. Bayonetta 3 is an invigorated sequel with fresh new ideas that embolden its 13-year-old combat system, an impressive amount of variety throughout its 10 to 12-hour campaign, and more of that trademark sexy Bayonetta style that makes the series one of a kind.

title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 review
description:
Modern Warfare 2's greatest strength is that it doesn't have a gimmick, because it doesn't need one.All Modern Warfare 2 needs to be is a great shooter, and it delivers. This is the Cal

Modern Warfare 2's greatest strength is that it doesn't have a gimmick, because it doesn't need one.

All Modern Warfare 2 needs to be is a great shooter, and it delivers. This is the Call of Duty experience, deconstructed, reconsidered, and obsessively optimized over 15 uninterrupted years of iteration. I know when I'm playing a Black Ops game because it has offbeat arcade modes and the latest iteration of Nuketown. I know I'm playing a Modern Warfare game because the shooting is so finely tuned that I want to take my Gunsmith build out to dinner. Infinity Ward has officially mastered the instant gratification of aiming down sights and deleting targets.

That goes a long way, though some of Modern Warfare 2's biggest swings, such as revamped progression and a genre-bending campaign, are less elegant. It also suffers from an obtuse UI, fits of crashes, weird bugs, and the unexplained absence of basic features like stat tracking. But altogether, it's a good year for Call of Duty.

title: Pokémon Scarlet and Violet Review - IGN

But from the moment I left the hallowed halls of Uva Academy, that promise has been wonderfully fulfilled, with open-world, open-ended gameplay serving as a shining beacon for the future of this beloved franchise. And yet, a finger on the cursed Mankey’s paw has curled anyway – Scarlet and Violet’s wonderfully innovative design is dramatically undermined by the numerous ways in which they feel deeply unfinished, with issues ranging from an incomplete world to massive and ubiquitous technical problems. So even though I want to celebrate how this generation reinvents and reinvigorates the world of Pokémon, I can’t without putting a great big warning label on it.

title: Marvel's Midnight Suns Review - IGN
description: One of my favorite things about watching superheroes duke it out is when someone gets smacked so hard they fly backwards and crash through solid walls, explode tanker trucks, or slam into their friends. It’s an awesome demonstration of just how strong these godlike characters are supposed to be, and it’s always a disappointment when a superhero game doesn’t quite capture that feeling. With Marvel’s Midnight Suns, however, Firaxis has built a deep and innovative turn-based tactical combat system around the joy of having Iron Man, Dr. Strange, Blade, and more knock enemies around like toys they're trying to break – and that hasn’t gotten old in the roughly 75 hours of its surprisingly expansive RPG campaign. A lot of that time isn’t spent in battles, though, and while it’s certainly appealing to get up close and personal with this cast of more than a dozen popular and lesser-known Marvel heroes, it does tend to go a bit overboard with convincing Earth’s mightiest heroes to all be your BFFs.

title: Hivemapper is 1M kilometers closer to goal of beating Google Maps
description:
Hivemapper relied on ride-hail, delivery and truck drivers with dash cams to collect 1 million unique kms of fresh map data.

Hivemapper, the startup that puts dashcams on ride-hail and delivery vehicles to map the world, is getting a little closer to its goal of toppling the B2B mapping empire that Google has built.

With only 2% of the world’s roads mapped, Hivemapper is still very much the underdog in this fight. But Gabe Nelson, Hivemapper’s head of operations, reckons the startup is reaching an inflection point that will lead to exponential scale.

Hivemapper said Thursday it collected more than 1 million kilometers (about 620,000 miles) of unique street-level imagery. Compared to Google’s 60 million kilometers, that’s small potatoes. However, Hivemapper collected this data over the last three months. It took Google from 2007 to 2019 to collect 16.1 million kilometers of unique road data.

Now the startup aims to map 10 million unique road kilometers by early next year.

Hivemapper relies on individual contributors around the world to collect its street-view data, rather than spending millions of dollars putting dedicated mapping vehicles on the road. Its dashcams are equipped with a high-quality imager and precise GPS, and they go for $549. Mapping with dashcams, the company says, means its data is continuously being refreshed, whereas much of Google’s Street View imagery, particularly outside of urban centers, is over a decade old.
longFormSummary:
• The TechCrunch article covers Hivemapper, a startup that pays ride-hail, delivery, and truck drivers to mount dashcams on their vehicles in order to build a street-level mapping dataset that competes with Google Maps.
  • As of the March 2023 announcement, Hivemapper had collected over 1 million unique kilometers of imagery in about three months, using a network of more than 11,000 contributors across 418 regions.
  • By comparison, Google has mapped roughly 60 million kilometers total, taking from 2007 to 2019 to reach 16.1 million kilometers of unique road data.
  • Hivemapper's dashcams cost $549 and use GPS plus imaging hardware; the company argues its crowdsourced approach keeps imagery continuously refreshed compared to Google's Street View data, some of which is over a decade old in non-urban areas.
  • Drivers are compensated in a token called HONEY, from a fixed total supply of 10 billion, and fleet operators get dashboards to track earnings; the company offers higher rewards in targeted regions including South Korea, the Netherlands, Portugal, London, Paris, Madrid, and Tokyo to accelerate coverage.
  • With only about 2% of the world's roads mapped so far, Hivemapper's next stated goal is to reach 10 million unique kilometers by early the following year.

title: Resident Evil 4 Review  - IGN

title: Street Fighter 6 is scheduled to release on June 2, 2023 on PC, Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation 5
description:
The next evolution of the Street Fighter series is almost here, focusing heavily on single-player elements to ensure there’s plenty of content for every level of fighter. Street Fighter 5 was heavily criticized at launch for its lack of playable content outside of versus mode and while this satisfied most high-level players, casual players found there was very little to keep them entertained.
Capcom has taken its time developing Street Fighter 6 to ensure they don’t repeat the same mistakes again. It features a brand new single-player story mode which gives players a chance to explore Metro City as a custom fighter. Street Fighter 6 is shaping up to become one of the best fighting games and potentially one of the best PC games overall.
longFormSummary:
• Street Fighter 6 launched on June 2, 2023 for PC, Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation 5 (it is not on Xbox Game Pass).
  • Capcom built the game around a new single-player World Tour mode that lets players explore Metro City as a custom fighter, marking the series' first real narrative progression since Street Fighter III: Third Strike more than 20 years earlier -- a direct response to criticism that Street Fighter V launched with too little content for casual players.
  • The game introduces a Modern control type that simplifies special moves and combos to single-button inputs for newcomers, alongside a unified Drive gauge powering five techniques (Drive Impact, Drive Parry, Drive Reversal, Drive Rush, and Overdrive Arts) revived and reworked from earlier games in the series.
  • A social Battle Hub lets players interact via avatars, play arcade cabinets featuring Capcom classics like Street Fighter Alpha 2 and Final Fight, join tournaments through an Event Counter, and customize their avatar in a Body Shop.
  • The game supports full crossplay across PlayStation, Xbox, and PC, with an option to disable it.

title: San Francisco's Millennium Tower Fix Declared a Success
description: Engineers completed a $100M underpinning project meant to arrest the sinking and tilt of San Francisco's Millennium Tower.
longFormSummary:
• The 58-storey Millennium Tower had sunk more than a foot and tilted around 30 inches to the northwest since opening in 2009, largely because its foundation wasn't anchored to bedrock.
  • The fix drove 18 new concrete piles down to bedrock around the building's perimeter and gradually shifted a portion of the tower's load onto them.
  • Work on the piles began in late 2020 and the load-transfer process finished in mid-2023, after an earlier design was paused and reworked.
  • Engineers reported that settlement had stopped and the building had even recovered a small amount of its lean, though full correction is expected to continue slowly for years.
address: 301 Mission Street, San Francisco, California, USA
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: the pile-driving and load-shifting project "was finished earlier this month," in an article published June 21, 2023.

title: Insider Shares More On Tesla's Project Highland AKA Model 3 Refresh
description:
Several test prototypes have already been spotted with camouflaged front and rear ends, suggesting the Model 3 is in for some major visual updates. But Tesla's compact sedan will get more than that. According to a "trusted insider" who offered an exclusive insight to Not A Tesla App, the Project Highland will bring significant changes inside and out. 

Starting with the design, the report notes the headlights will have a different shape, which means the front bumper will be redesigned as well. It will be more aerodynamic and will now house a single camera in the center area of the lower grille, in similar fashion to the Cybertruck.

Out back, the refreshed Tesla Model 3 is also getting a redesigned bumper, although the changes will likely be purely for aesthetic reasons.

The source also said the side mirrors will be subtly updated and the Project Highland will be getting more cameras to take advantage of the new Hardware 4.0 Autopilot supercomputer. Three new cameras will reportedly be added to the Model 3: one in the center of the front bumper and two on the sides of the car.

title: Elon Musk announces timing for Tesla Cybertruck delivery event

Based on the launch of Tesla’s most recent models, especially the Model Y, we should expect Tesla to only deliver a few Cybertrucks during the delivery event, likely only to Tesla insiders, and we can expect months between the event and the start of deliveries to customers.

Interestingly, Musk also said that Cybertruck reservation holders should expect to get an update on specs and pricing at that event at the end of Q3.

title: Sagrada Família Tower of Jesus Christ Completed
description: Barcelona's basilica tops out its 172.5-metre central tower, making it the world's tallest church, timed for the centenary of Antoni Gaudí's death. Estimated date.
longFormSummary:
• The Sagrada Família is Antoni Gaudí's Catholic basilica in Barcelona's Eixample district, under construction since 1882 and consecrated as a minor basilica by Pope Benedict XVI in 2010.
  • Gaudí took over the design in 1883, blending Gothic and Art Nouveau styles with tree-like columns, hyperboloid surfaces, and three grand façades (Nativity, Passion, and Glory); when he died in 1926 the building was only 15-25% complete.
  • Construction was set back further when anarchists destroyed part of the structure and his original plans during the 1936 Spanish Civil War; work resumed in the 1950s and accelerated with computer-aided design, funded entirely by private donations and visitor entrance fees, with an annual construction budget of around €25 million.
  • The basilica surpassed Ulm Minster to become the world's tallest church at 162.91 meters in October 2025, and its central Tower of Jesus Christ reached its full designed height of 172.5 meters in February 2026.
  • Pope Leo XIV blessed and inaugurated the completed tower on June 10, 2026, timed to coincide with the centenary of Gaudí's death, though decorative elements and interior spires are expected to continue until around 2028-2032.

title: Co-Owners Scrap the €800M Tour Montparnasse Overhaul
description: Ten years after Paris approved Nouvelle AOM's full glass-facade transformation of the Tour Montparnasse, the tower's co-owners voted to abandon that plan in favour of a smaller, cheaper intervention.
longFormSummary:
• Completed in 1973, the Tour Montparnasse is still the only skyscraper inside central Paris; the backlash to it led France to ban tall buildings in the city centre just four years later.
  • In 2017 Paris approved a Nouvelle AOM-designed renovation meant to strip the tower to its frame and wrap it in transparent glazing and sky gardens, with tenants vacating by March 2026 ahead of construction.
  • Discovered asbestos and rising costs pushed the budget from an original €624 million toward €800 million, and at a 21 July 2026 general assembly, co-owner LFPI refused further funding, killing the original design.
  • Asbestos removal and partial facade work are still going ahead from September 2026, while architects are now tasked with designing a cheaper version before the building permit lapses in November 2026.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "co-owners of the tower voted to scrap the ambitious transformation" at a 21 July 2026 general assembly.

title: Gordie Howe International Bridge Opens
description: A 853-metre cable-stayed span over the Detroit River, the longest in North America, carrying the busiest US-Canada trade corridor. Estimated date.
longFormSummary:
• The Gordie Howe International Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge connecting Detroit, Michigan to Windsor, Ontario across the Detroit River, named for the hockey legend, with twin 220-meter towers shaped to evoke a hockey stick mid-slapshot.
  • The 2.5 km structure has an 853-meter main span, the longest cable-stayed span in North America, supported by 216 cable stays, and carries six automotive lanes plus a pedestrian and bicycle path 46 meters above the water.
  • It was funded entirely by the Canadian federal government at a cost of roughly CA$6.4 billion.
  • It is intended to relieve the nearby Ambassador Bridge, which currently carries about a quarter of all US-Canada truck traffic, by giving Interstate 75 a direct, uninterrupted connection to Highway 401 without routing through city streets, supporting bilateral automotive trade that reached US$51 billion in 2023 and serving roughly 5,000 Canadian commuters who work in Detroit daily.
  • Construction ran from June 2018 to June 2026, with the bridge inaugurated on July 24, 2026 and opened to traffic on July 27, 2026, well behind its original 2024 target due to COVID-19 and other delays.

title: Glacier Collapse Destroys the Rasuwagadhi Border Crossing
description: A chunk of the Langtang Lirung glacier breaks off 5 km up the valley and grows into a debris flow that wipes out the Nepal–China border crossing, its bridges, and a 111 MW hydropower plant.
longFormSummary:
• A roughly 0.2 km² mass of ice and rock broke off Langtang Lirung at about 5.2 km elevation and fell some 1.2 km to the valley floor, turning meltwater and debris into a flow survivors described as "a wall of water" by the time it reached Rasuwagadhi.
  • The flood destroyed the Rasuwagadhi/Gyirong Port border crossing, the Nepal–China bridge, roughly 69 km of road and dozens of smaller bridges, and swept away the 111 MW Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Plant, leaving dozens of its workers missing.
  • It struck the same Nepal–Tibet crossing about thirteen months after a comparable glacier-triggered flood hit the Rasuwa district in July 2025.

title: Western Sydney International Airport Opens
description: Sydney's second international gateway at Badgerys Creek begins commercial flights, built with a 24-hour curfew-free runway. Estimated date.

title: Auckland City Rail Link Opens
description: Twin 3.45 km tunnels turning Britomart from a dead-end terminus into a through station, doubling rail capacity. Estimated date.

• Auckland's City Rail Link is a pair of 3.45-kilometer underground tunnels running beneath Albert Street and the city center, extending the rail network from Waitematā station (formerly Britomart) to Maungawhau station (formerly Mount Eden) and adding two intermediate stations, Te Waihorotiu near Aotea Square and Karanga-a-Hape near Karangahape Road.

title: BepiColombo Enters Mercury Orbit

title: Thirty Meter Telescope Decision Deadline
description: A 30-metre segmented-mirror telescope stalled for a decade by opposition to building on Mauna Kea, with La Palma as the alternate site. Estimated date.
longFormSummary:
• The Thirty Meter Telescope is a proposed extremely large telescope with a 30-meter primary mirror made of 492 hexagonal segments, offering nine times the light-gathering power of the Keck Observatory and covering wavelengths from near-ultraviolet to mid-infrared with adaptive optics.
  • Its planned site atop Mauna Kea in Hawaii, considered the most sacred mountain in Hawaiian culture, has drawn sustained Native Hawaiian protests since 2014.
  • Hawaii's Supreme Court invalidated the original 2011 construction permit in December 2015 over procedural violations, a revised permit was approved in 2018, and blockades in 2014-2015 and a four-week standoff in July 2019 repeatedly halted construction, which has been stalled since 2015.
  • La Palma in Spain's Canary Islands was proposed as a backup site after the 2019 protests, though astronomers consider it scientifically inferior due to atmospheric water vapor interfering with mid-infrared observations, and a Spanish court revoked land concessions there in 2021 before the issue was resolved by 2023.
  • In June 2025, the U.S. National Science Foundation withdrew its support for the project in favor of the competing Giant Magellan Telescope, and while the international TMT consortium says it intends to proceed, the project's future funding remains highly uncertain.

title: Halley's Comet Returns to Perihelion

longFormSummary:

  • It follows a highly elliptical, retrograde orbit lasting 74 to 79 years, swinging from a perihelion of just 0.59 astronomical units from the Sun out to an aphelion of 35 AU, nearly reaching Pluto's orbit.
  • Its appearances have been recorded since at least 240 BC in Chinese records, and its 1066 passage is depicted on the Bayeux Tapestry.
  • English astronomer Edmond Halley established its periodicity in 1705 by matching observations from 1531, 1607, and 1682, correctly predicting its return in 1758.
